errors.evidence: The description is slightly incomplete. The chart shows the distribution of counts for different polarity scores, not just the distribution of the scores themselves.

While the y-axis tick labels go up to 8000, the data peak clearly exceeds this value, reaching approximately 9000. Stating the range is 0 to 8000 is misleading as it incorrectly implies 8000 is the maximum value on the chart.

errors.text_span: beginning at a count of approximately 40 at a polarity score of -1.0
errors.evidence: The data point at a polarity score of -1.0 has a count value of 0, not approximately 40.

errors.text_span: a maximum count of approximately 7800 at a polarity score of 0.1
errors.evidence: The description incorrectly identifies both the value and location of the peak. The maximum count is approximately 9000 (not 7800), and it occurs at a polarity score slightly above 0.0, not at 0.1.

errors.text_span: then decreases to a count of approximately 1800 at a polarity score of 0.6.
errors.evidence: This description drastically oversimplifies the trend after the main peak, completely omitting a significant secondary peak at a polarity score of 0.2 (count ~5200) and a third peak at 0.5 (count ~1800). It also incorrectly reports the final point; at a polarity score of 0.6, the count is near 0, not 1800.
